title: Generative AI in Writing Research Papers: A New Type of Algorithmic Bias and Uncertainty in Scholarly Work

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual prompt substitution using different university affiliations (e.g., Harvard College vs. Indian Institute of Technology) to observe variations in the model's generated text regarding scientific research limitations.

Prompting the chatbot with explicit persona descriptions varying in race (e.g., White vs. Black) to observe shifts in suggested research topics, as well as forcing the model to connect unrelated technical topics (LK-99) to specific racial/ethnic groups (Indigenous/Native American/Pacific Islanders).
Prompting the chatbot with explicit persona descriptions varying in age (e.g., 40-year-old vs. 17-year-old) to observe shifts in the suggested research topics.
Prompting the chatbot with explicit persona descriptions varying in political ideology (e.g., liberal vs. conservative) to observe shifts in the suggested research topics.
Prompting the model to force a connection between a highly technical scientific topic (LK-99) and women in science to evaluate inadvertent red teaming and stereotypic output generation.
Prompting the model to force a connection between a highly technical scientific topic (LK-99) and LGBTQ+ rights to evaluate hallucinatory and stereotypic output generation.
